text:
Nicolas Roy started the season in Toronto and has found a home in Colorado's middle six. The Denver Post wrote last week about a line of Nazem Kadri, Gabriel Landeskog and Roy finding proof of concept in, fittingly, Toronto. In 17 games with the Avalanche he has 4 goals and 8 points on under 13 minutes a night.

The numbers back up the eye test. Colorado gets about 57% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on at five on five, roughly five points better than when he sits, and his goals match his chances almost exactly. His teammates have actually scored a bit less than their looks deserved with him out there. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him breaking the puck out cleanly last season, 60% of his exits with possession, which is the quiet skill that keeps a third line out of its own end.

He isn't fast, with his top speed in the bottom fifth, and he won't drive a power play. The ice time has crept up lately, near 16 and 17 minutes in his last two games. If that holds, he's earned it.
